Thanks Jules — answers inline and a recommended path forward below.

1) Private/on-prem timeline and blockers
- Typical timeline: 8–12 weeks for a standard on-prem deployment (network, infra, installation, KMS/HSM integration, and acceptance testing).
- Main blockers we see: firewall/VPN provisioning, HSM certificate exchange, and customer change-control windows for production network access.

2) Dedicated pilot and pricing
- We can offer a 6-week dedicated pilot in a reserved pool at a reduced pilot rate. Hosted (no commit) is our fastest path (~provision in 48–72 hours) but has higher per-token unit costs; Dedicated commit reduces unit costs by ~30–45% depending on throughput. Ballpark numbers: Hosted: $XX per 1M tokens; Dedicated reserve: starting at $15k/month for predictable capacity; Private: one-time infra + license typically a 6-figure project depending on scale. We will provide a formal quote once you confirm capacity target (tokens/sec and average seq length).

3) Data flow and logs
- In Hosted and Dedicated: inference requests, prefix/KV cache, and ephemeral logs are retained per agreed retention in the MAP; we do NOT use customer data for training. KV cache is in GPU process memory, not persisted except for optional export. Audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM via secure syslog/S3.

Next steps (recommended)
- Week of Nov 1: Redwood to run two short evals — p95 latency on a sample prompt set and quantized accuracy check (Priyom will run these).
- Nov 3: Redwood to share a short Delta Doc listing configuration differences between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for Cerebellum workloads (Marcus).
- Nov 8: Decision call / acceptance gate prep (30 minutes) to confirm procurement path; finalize MAP and signature.

We've attached the SOC2 snapshot (SOC2-evidence-redwood.pdf) and linked the HubSpot MAP record here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/CE-2026-0987.

If that schedule works, I'll draft the canary run plan and a condensed quote for Procurement.

Best,
Stephanie
